You are scouting for places where TypeSafe's Jev model would give real leverage in Eric Rash's (Baylor Applied Performance) RESEARCH and PROGRAM projects. Root: C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV. Start with RESEARCH.md and PROGRAM.md (area indexes), then the relevant folders: Weekly_Research_Review, SportScienceResearchRepo, ZoteroInjestion, LibraryProject, BookInbox, BookVaultApp, TOS_Evidence_Brief, May_Meetings_Research, Epilepsy-Baseball-Research, GameONPaper, Sport_Tech_Vetting, SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework, SoftwareTechDocs, Tech_Inventory_Analysis, TechEd_Prop, Supervisor_Reviews, OKRs_2026-27, NCAA_BestPractices_Doc, Education_Alignment_Initiative, Education_Content_Agent, Intern_Curriculum, CPSS_BaylorSportScience_Curriculum, Department_Audits, AppliedNewsletter_2026, BAIR_Steering_Committee, SportScience_Benchmarking, Performance_Playbook, Program_Context_Meet, SpecialRequests, SPA_Presentation, etc. Read each project's docs/STATUS.md and CLAUDE.md/README first, then peek at data/code. Excerpts, not whole files.

What Jev is: a cloud API that takes text/JSON "state" plus typed questions and returns calibrated answers — Noul (P(yes)), Choice (pick one of ≤240 options, with probabilities), Score (position on a 2–10 level rubric). ~100ms, very cheap ($0.042/M tokens; 1,018 papers classified for $0.08). It does NOT generate text, is bad at arithmetic/counting/dates/numeric thresholds. Best moves: select-don't-generate, split one fuzzy judgment into many narrow questions and combine them with weights set in code, rubric scoring, turn free text into features, verify claims against a source document, find the answering line in a policy document (semantic_find), rerank.

ALREADY BUILT or DECIDED — do not re-propose: Zotero topic classification with confidence backoff (live, 1,418 records); citation/deliverable verifier on Research in 5 + status report (live); Zotero renames (skip, nothing reads the labels); semantic_find over Kitman/MyLink contracts (blocked, contracts not on disk).

GATE every candidate must pass: (1) the judgment is genuinely fuzzy/semantic; (2) something ALREADY consumes the answer; (3) you can state the current deterministic/manual baseline and why it falls short.

Hunt specifically for: survey free-text responses (e.g., the Tech Inventory survey had 52 responses — are there open-ended answers being hand-coded?), vendor vetting against rubrics (Sport_Tech_Vetting — scoring vendor docs/demos on criteria), curriculum/course alignment mapping (map content to competencies/standards — a Choice over a standards list), audit checklists judged against evidence docs, NCAA best-practice document gap checks, OKR key-result grading, paper triage/screening for systematic reviews (inclusion/exclusion criteria per abstract), book library tagging, newsletter content selection. Note which have real volume (dozens-thousands of items) vs one-offs.

Return (max ~700 words): a ranked list of up to 6 candidates. For each: project + file paths, the exact fuzzy judgment, the data (size, example), the consumer, the current baseline and its weakness, pass/fail per gate, and effort S/M/L. Also list 2–3 near-misses that fail the gate and why. Cite evidence.

# Advisor Tool

You have access to an `advisor` tool backed by a stronger reviewer model. It takes NO parameters -- when you call advisor(), your entire conversation history is automatically forwarded. They see the task, every tool call you've made, every result you've seen.

Call advisor BEFORE substantive work -- before writing, before committing to an interpretation, before building on an assumption. If the task requires orientation first (finding files, fetching a source, seeing what's there), do that, then call advisor. Orientation is not substantive work. Writing, editing, and declaring an answer are.

Also call advisor:

On tasks longer than a few steps, call advisor at least once before committing to an approach and once before declaring done. On short reactive tasks where the next action is dictated by tool output you just read, you don't need to keep calling -- the advisor adds most of its value on the first call, before the approach crystallizes.

Give the advice serious weight. If you follow a step and it fails empirically, or you have primary-source evidence that contradicts a specific claim (the file says X, the paper states Y), adapt. A passing self-test is not evidence the advice is wrong -- it's evidence your test doesn't check what the advice is checking.

This is a READ-ONLY exploration task. You are STRICTLY PROHIBITED from:

- Deleting files (no rm or deletion)
- Moving or copying files (no mv or cp)

- Running ANY commands that change system state

Your role is EXCLUSIVELY to search and analyze existing code. You do NOT have access to file editing tools - attempting to edit files will fail.

- Searching code and text with powerful regex patterns
- Reading and analyzing file contents

- Use Grep for searching file contents with regex
- Use Read when you know the specific file path you need to read
- Use Bash ONLY for read-only operations (ls, git status, git log, git diff, find, cat, head, tail)
- NEVER use Bash for: mkdir, touch, rm, cp, mv, git add, git commit, npm install, pip install, or any file creation/modification

- Communicate your final report directly as a regular message - do NOT attempt to create files

NOTE: You are meant to be a fast agent that returns output as quickly as possible. In order to achieve this you must:

Complete the user's search request efficiently and report your findings clearly.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

schema.name: Glob
schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),

(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See

here cover composing, listing, fetching, and rendering projects… [truncated]

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

## remarkable
# reMarkable MCP Server

Access documents from your reMarkable tablet. All operations are read-only.

## Available Tools

- `remarkable_browse(path, query)` - Browse folders or search for documents
- `remarkable_read(document, content_type, page, grep)` - Read document content with pagination
- `remarkable_recent(limit)` - Get recently modified documents
- `remarkable_status()` - Check connection and diagnose issues
- `remarkable_image(document, page, include_ocr)` - Get a PNG image with optional OCR

## Recommended Workflows

### Finding and Reading Documents
1. Use `remarkable_browse(query="keyword")` to search by name
2. Use `remarkable_read("Document Name")` to get content
3. Use `remarkable_read("Document", page=2)` to continue reading long documents
4. Use `remarkable_read("Document", grep="pattern")` to search within a document

### Getting Page Images
Use `remarkable_image` when you need visual context:
- Hand-drawn diagrams, sketches, or UI mockups
- Content that text extraction might miss
- Implementing designs based on hand-drawn wireframes

Example: `remarkable_image("UI Mockup", page=1)` returns a PNG image
Example: `remarkable_image("Notes", include_ocr=True)` returns image with extracted text

### For Large Documents
Use pagination to avoid overwhelming context. The response includes:
- `page` / `total_pages` - current position
- `more` - true if more content exists
- `next_page` - page number to request next

### Combining Tools
- Browse → Read: Find documents first, then read them
- Recent → Read: Check what was recently modified, then read specific ones
- Read with grep: Search for specific content within large documents
- Browse → Image: Find a document then get its visual representation

## MCP Resources

Documents are registered as resources for direct access:
- `remarkable:///{path}.txt` - Get full extracted text content in one request
- `remarkableimg:///{path}.page-{N}.png` - Get PNG image of page N (notebooks only)
- Use resources when you need complete document content without pagination… [truncated]

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

# reMarkable MCP Server

Access documents from your reMarkable tablet. All operations are read-only.

## Available Tools

- `remarkable_browse(path, query)` - Browse folders or search for documents
- `remarkable_read(document, content_type, page, grep)` - Read document content with pagination
- `remarkable_recent(limit)` - Get recently modified documents
- `remarkable_status()` - Check connection and diagnose issues
- `remarkable_image(document, page, include_ocr)` - Get a PNG image with optional OCR

## Recommended Workflows

### Finding and Reading Documents
1. Use `remarkable_browse(query="keyword")` to search by name
2. Use `remarkable_read("Document Name")` to get content
3. Use `remarkable_read("Document", page=2)` to continue reading long documents
4. Use `remarkable_read("Document", grep="pattern")` to search within a document

### Getting Page Images
Use `remarkable_image` when you need visual context:
- Hand-drawn diagrams, sketches, or UI mockups
- Content that text extraction might miss
- Implementing designs based on hand-drawn wireframes

Example: `remarkable_image("UI Mockup", page=1)` returns a PNG image
Example: `remarkable_image("Notes", include_ocr=True)` returns image with extracted text

### For Large Documents
Use pagination to avoid overwhelming context. The response includes:
- `page` / `total_pages` - current position
- `more` - true if more content exists
- `next_page` - page number to request next

### Combining Tools
- Browse → Read: Find documents first, then read them
- Recent → Read: Check what was recently modified, then read specific ones
- Read with grep: Search for specific content within large documents
- Browse → Image: Find a document then get its visual representation

## MCP Resources

Documents are registered as resources for direct access:
- `remarkable:///{path}.txt` - Get full extracted text content in one request
- `remarkableimg:///{path}.page-{N}.png` - Get PNG image of page N (notebooks only)
- Use resources when you need complete document content without pagination… [truncated]

# RESEARCH — area index

Literature, citation library, and reading pipelines. The grounded-evidence
layer behind the applied work.

## Projects

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `SportScienceResearchRepo/` | Main research repo. Has `CONTEXT.md`, a spec sheet, and an `index.html` micro-app → own `CLAUDE.md` |
| `ZoteroInjestion/` | Zotero ingest pipeline (~1,850 files). Note the spelling — "Injestion", not "Ingestion". |
| `LibraryProject/` | Book library → advisor entries → own `CLAUDE.md` |
| `Weekly_Research_Review/` | "Research in 5": weekly one-paper review. Deck PDF for Teams, post, email, running index. Outputs on `_DRIVE/07_EDUCATION/Research_in_5` → own `AGENTS.md` |
| `Epilepsy-Baseball-Research/` | Epilepsy + baseball literature review |
| `BookInbox/` | Staging for books not yet ingested |
| `reMarkale_extract/` | reMarkable highlight extraction. Note the spelling — "reMarkale". |
| `ContextVault/` | Context storage experiment |
| `May_Meetings_Research/` | May 2026 meeting materials and EOY research reporting. Disk is the source of truth → own `CLAUDE.md`. Dormant. |

## Tooling that serves this area

- Skills: `sports-science-research-grounding`, `library-advisor`,
  `ingest-book`, `ingest-resource`, `pp-zotero-research-library`
- CLIs: `zotero-research-library-pp-cli`, `zotero-research-library-pp-mcp`
- MCP: `zotero` (the one server in local `~/.claude.json`)
- Vault: `~/SecondBrain` holds 842 notes and has its own `CLAUDE.md`
- Compiled knowledge: `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/knowledge/` (185 articles)

## Notes

- Search across everything with `memsearch search "<query>" --top-k 5`
  rather than reading the knowledge index directly.
- Zotero recall gotcha: `project_milvus-lock-misdiagnosis.md`.
# PROGRAM — area index

Staff-facing work: reporting up, curriculum, proposals, vetting, and
department documents. Reports and decks, not pipelines.

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Program_Context_Meet/` | Meeting context prep → own `CLAUDE.md` |
| `SpecialRequests/` | One-off asks from staff |

The biweekly status report for Kenny Boyd and Chris Ruf runs from the
`status-report` skill. Sourcing rules: `project_status-report-sourcing.md`.

## Curriculum and education

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `CPSS_BaylorSportScience_Curriculum/` | Sport science curriculum → own `CLAUDE.md` |
| `Education_Content_Agent/` | Education content generation → own `CLAUDE.md` |
| `TechEd_Prop/` | Tech education proposal |
| `RTP_Constraints_Course/` | Constraints-led return-to-performance course for Joe Smith, plus a planned drill-design tool → own `CLAUDE.md` |
| `RTP_DataCollection_Talk/` | Return-to-play data collection talk |
| `TSSHB_Skills/` | Skills doc. Empty. |
| `Performance_Playbook/` | Departmental user manual: intern SOPs and education materials → own `AGENTS.md` + `docs/context.md`. Disk is the source of truth; the Cowork project is only a pointer. Holds ~33 MB of binary Office/PDF templates, so commit on structural change, not every edit. |

## Frameworks, vetting, and policy

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Department_Audits/` | Executable sport performance departmental audit playbooks → own `AGENTS.md` + `docs/context.md`. Disk is the source of truth; the Cowork project is only a pointer. Bulk source materials still live in Google Drive. |
| `SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/` | Software and tech management framework |
| `Sport_Tech_Vetting/` | Vetting process for sport tech vendors |
| `Transformative_Athlete_Experience/` | Athlete experience initiative |
| `NCAA_BestPractices_Doc/` | NCAA best practices. Empty. |

## Brand and house style

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Baylor_Doc_Style/` | Document style rules |
| `Baylor_Fonts/` | Approved typefaces |

## People and planning

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Baseball_JD/` | Job description draft |
| `Linda Projects/` | Collaborator project folder. Note the space in the name. |
| `OKRs_2026-27/` | OKR folder. Empty — the live v3 doc lives elsewhere. |
| `SPA_Presentation/` | Presentation. Empty. |

## Notes

- Doc review preferences: `project_kenny-boyd-doc-review-preferences.md`.
- Deck series: use `five-slides-generator` for "5 Slides in 5 Minutes".
- Dormant/empty here: `TSSHB_Skills`, `NCAA_BestPractices_Doc`,
  `OKRs_2026-27`, `SPA_Presentation`.

# Tech_Inventory_Analysis

Cleaning and analysis of the Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory survey.

Companion to `~/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework`, which holds the framework
documents, the form specs, and the form links. This folder holds only the
collected data and what comes out of it.

## Layout

```
raw/     frozen survey exports, date-stamped. never edited.
scripts/ clean_inventory.py (parser) + aliases.py (all judgement calls)
clean/   generated CSVs. delete and regenerate freely.
docs/    findings
deliverables/  anything that goes to Kenny / Jon Allen / ITS
```

## Run

```bash
cd ~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis
uv run --with openpyxl python3 scripts/clean_inventory.py
```

The script reads the newest `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx` and rewrites
everything in `clean/`. It is safe to run repeatedly.

Then rebuild the three documents. All read `clean/*.csv`, so none can drift
from the data, and all are set in the shared house style from
`~/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style` (found at `~/DEV/` on the Mac or `~/Desktop/DEV/` on
Windows, or wherever `BAYLOR_DOC_STYLE` points):

```bash
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python scripts/build_docx.py
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python scripts/build_exec_summary.py
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python scripts/build_tech_lists.py
```

Filenames and dates come from the newest `raw/` export. On Windows the scripts
drive Word through COM and do not need it open;

# Tech_Inventory_Analysis

Cleaning and analysis of the Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory survey.

Companion to `~/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework`, which holds the framework
documents, the form specs, and the form links. This folder holds only the
collected data and what comes out of it.

## Layout

```
raw/     frozen survey exports, date-stamped. never edited.
scripts/ clean_inventory.py (parser) + aliases.py (all judgement calls)
clean/   generated CSVs. delete and regenerate freely.
docs/    findings
deliverables/  anything that goes to Kenny / Jon Allen / ITS
```

## Run

```bash
cd ~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis
uv run --with openpyxl python3 scripts/clean_inventory.py
```

The script reads the newest `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx` and rewrites
everything in `clean/`. It is safe to run repeatedly.

Then rebuild the three documents. All read `clean/*.csv`, so none can drift
from the data, and all are set in the shared house style from
`~/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style` (found at `~/DEV/` on the Mac or `~/Desktop/DEV/` on
Windows, or wherever `BAYLOR_DOC_STYLE` points):

```bash
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python scripts/build_docx.py
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python scripts/build_exec_summary.py
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python scripts/build_tech_lists.py
```

Filenames and dates come from the newest `raw/` export. On Windows the scripts
drive Word through COM and do not need it open;

# B.A.I.R. Steering Committee

Baylor Athletics Innovation & Research. Research governance for the department:
the proposal review framework, the evaluation criteria, and the active study pipeline.

## Repo layout

Mirrors the `04_RESEARCH` structure on the primary storage drive:

- `01_Process/` — the review process itself, criteria, templates, workflow docs
- `02_Proposals/` — submissions, organized as Under_Review / Approved / Declined_or_Deferred
- `04_Committee/` — committee membership, meeting materials, minutes, decisions

Not copied here (they live on the drive and are either large, in flux, or outside
governance scope): `03_Active_Studies`, `05_Reporting`, `06_Grants`, `07_Admin_Tools`,
`_INBOX`, `_Archive`, `_Mark_for_Deletion`.

Source: `04_RESEARCH` on the primary storage drive.

## Conventions

- New studies land in `04_RESEARCH\_INBOX` on the drive first, then get filed
- Proposals move between the three `02_Proposals` subfolders as decisions are made;
  a proposal is never deleted, only moved to Declined_or_Deferred
- Committee decisions get written down in `04_Committee`, not left in email

## Related

- S2_Evaluation, ForcePlate_DecisionSystem, RTP_WorkingGroup (studies in the pipeline)
- Education_Alignment_Initiative (shares the B.A.I.R. umbrella)

# B.A.I.R. Steering Committee

Baylor Athletics Innovation & Research. Research governance for the department:
the proposal review framework, the evaluation criteria, and the active study pipeline.

## Repo layout

Mirrors the `04_RESEARCH` structure on the primary storage drive:

- `01_Process/` — the review process itself, criteria, templates, workflow docs
- `02_Proposals/` — submissions, organized as Under_Review / Approved / Declined_or_Deferred
- `04_Committee/` — committee membership, meeting materials, minutes, decisions

Not copied here (they live on the drive and are either large, in flux, or outside
governance scope): `03_Active_Studies`, `05_Reporting`, `06_Grants`, `07_Admin_Tools`,
`_INBOX`, `_Archive`, `_Mark_for_Deletion`.

Source: `04_RESEARCH` on the primary storage drive.

## Conventions

- New studies land in `04_RESEARCH\_INBOX` on the drive first, then get filed
- Proposals move between the three `02_Proposals` subfolders as decisions are made;
  a proposal is never deleted, only moved to Declined_or_Deferred
- Committee decisions get written down in `04_Committee`, not left in email

## Related

- S2_Evaluation, ForcePlate_DecisionSystem, RTP_WorkingGroup (studies in the pipeline)
- Education_Alignment_Initiative (shares the B.A.I.R. umbrella)

# Baylor Athletics Health & Performance Evidence

Shared language for curating health and performance evidence and translating it into practical decision support for Baylor Athletics staff.

## Language

**Evidence Library**:
A curated collection of source-grounded evidence resources approved for staff discovery and synthesis.
_Avoid_: Paper archive, research database

**Evidence Library Publication Candidate**:
A source-verified synthesis proposed for admission to the Evidence Library. It requires accountable review,
duplicate and taxonomy checks, and stable-ID assignment before publication.
_Avoid_: Published paper, submission, automatic import

**Ask the Library**:
The decision-support experience that converts a staff question into a structured Decision Brief grounded in the Evidence Library.
_Avoid_: Chatbot, answer engine

**Decision Brief**:
A structured, source-grounded synthesis that states the bottom line, applicability, evidence confidence, limitations, practical options and guardrails, and supporting sources. It informs staff judgment rather than making the final decision.
_Avoid_: Definitive answer, prescription

**Brief Revision**:
A new version of a Decision Brief created after its requester changes the Practical Question or Decision Context. It preserves the prior version rather than extending an open-ended chat transcript or silently rewriting the brief.
_Avoid_: Follow-up chat, in-place overwrite

**Operational View**:
The concise default presentation of a Decision Brief, designed for approximately two minutes of reading and focused on direction, confidence, action, guardrails, and critical caveats. Research detail remains available through expandable evidence sections.
_Avoid_: Abstract, full research report

**Library-Grounded**:
A claim or conclusion supported only by evidence resources in the Evidence Library, with the supporting sources made traceable.
_Avoid_: Generally research-backed, AI-generated

**Source-Grounded Claim**:
A substantive statement supported by the original text of an Evidence Library source. Existing summaries and taxonomy may locate the source but cannot serve as the claim's sole support.
_Avoid_: Summary-grounded claim, unsupported citation

**Coverage Gap**:
An explicit finding that the Evidence Library does not contain enough relevant evidence to support a Decision Brief. It does not mean that an intervention is ineffective or that no external evidence exists.
_Avoid_:

# Education Content Agent

Turns a topic and an angle into finished education content for Baylor Athletics
Applied Performance — a researched, sourced brief, then a "5 Slides in 5 Minutes" deck
and a printed one-pager built from it.

```
topic + your angle
        │
        ▼
  content-researcher ──> briefs/YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md    a sourced fact sheet, no slides
        │
        ▼
  content-writer ──┬──> deck outline  ──> five-slides-generator skill ──> .pptx
                   └──> one-pager     ──> html-to-pdf skill           ──> .pdf
```

## Why this exists

Applied Performance is one person. The staff deck series stalled, and it stalled at the
expensive step: researching a topic properly and writing it into a narrative. Building
the `.pptx` was never the bottleneck — a skill already does that.

So this project take
######## Education_Content_Agent/PRODUCT.md
# PRODUCT.md

## What this is

A content engine for Baylor Athletics Applied Performance staff education. A topic and an
angle go in; a sourced research brief comes out; house-format content is written from that
brief. Its output is the "5 Slides in 5 Minutes" series.

## The unique mechanism

Research once, publish many. The expensive step in this department is not building a deck,
it is establishing what is actually true about a topic and where the evidence runs out. A
brief is written once, every number carries a source, and every format is written from that
one brief. Two decks can never quietly disagree because there is only one set of facts.

## Who it is for

**The presenter:** Eric, Director of Applied Performance. One person covering every sport,
no protected time. The series stalled after a handful of decks because writing them cost
hours he does not have.

######## Education_Content_Agent/PRODUCT.md
# PRODUCT.md

## What this is

A content engine for Baylor Athletics Applied Performance staff education. A topic and an
angle go in; a sourced research brief comes out; house-format content is written from that
brief. Its output is the "5 Slides in 5 Minutes" series.

## The unique mechanism

Research once, publish many. The expensive step in this department is not building a deck,
it is establishing what is actually true about a topic and where the evidence runs out. A
brief is written once, every number carries a source, and every format is written from that
one brief. Two decks can never quietly disagree because there is only one set of facts.

## Who it is for

**The presenter:** Eric, Director of Applied Performance. One person covering every sport,
no protected time. The series stalled after a handful of decks because writing them cost
hours he does not have.

## What this is

The recurring bi-weekly time and progress update Eric sends to leadership,
plus the handoff that describes how to write one.

## Where the files live

Everything is here in the repo. Sent copies, if kept, go on Google Drive at
``08_ADMIN\Supervisor_Reviews``.

## Session routine

- Start: run `git pull`, then read `docs/STATUS.md` before doing anything else.
- End: update `docs/STATUS.md` (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions

- Durable notes and decisions go in `docs/`, committed. Not in chat.
- Documents, data exports and deliverables live on the primary storage drive
  (Google Drive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive`), not in this repo. Files over
  95 MB never go in git.
- Third-party platforms (VALD Hub, Telemetry, Teamworks) are read-only.
- Never paste credentials into chat. Read them from files and never echo them.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.

## Handling care

These are internal work updates. Keep other people out of them beyond what the
update itself requires.

7:## Jev in one screen
14:| Type | Answers | Returns |
15:|---|---|---|
16:| `Noul` | Is this statement true? | `noul`, a probability from 0 to 1. No separate confidence. |
17:| `Choice` | Which of these options? | `choice`, `probabilities` over every option, `confidence` |
18:| `Score` | Which level on this rubric? | `score` (can land between levels), `legend`, `probabilities`, `confidence` |
39:## Limits and failure modes
43:| Limit | Value |
44:|---|---|
45:| Price | $0.042 per million input tokens. Output tokens free. |
46:| Context | 64k per request; 32k for `state` plus the longest question |
47:| Choice options | 255 maximum, roughly 240 before reliability drops |
48:| Score levels | 2 minimum, 10 maximum. An 11th returns a server error. |
49:| Input | Text only. String, JSON object, or array. No image, audio, video. |
50:| Rate | 250,000 tokens/sec, 1,200 requests/min, adjusted without notice |
51:| Latency | About 100 to 115 ms per call, measured across two cookbooks |
52:| Language | English is best. Other languages accepted, lower accuracy. |

# Zotero backlog classification

Second item in the capability map's sequence, after the skill router. Every research
record in the Zotero library gets a topic; when Jev is not confident enough to name
one, it reports the broader domain that topic sits in instead. Nothing is dropped and
nothing queues for review.

Built 2026-09-19 from the `classification_using_confidence` cookbook
(`docs/vendor/typesafe/cookbooks/classification_using_confidence.md`). Code in
`zotero_classify/`.

**Governance: tier A.** Published literature and its metadata only. No athlete data,
no health records, nothing from GPS, force plate, DEXA or S2. The state sent to the
API is a title, a journal, a year and up to 2,000 characters of a published abstract.

| | |
|---|---|
| records classified | **1,418** — every eligible research item, reconciled against the bridge's own count |
| named a specific topic | **1,236 (87%)** |
| reported as a domain instead | 182 (13%) |
| taxonomy | 96 topics in 14 domains |
| wall time | **86 seconds**, 8 workers, zero failures |
| cost | about **$0.07** at $0.042 per million input tokens, output free |

> **ANSWERED 2026-09-20 — `sde_cascade` is a CODE LINTER, not a Jev build.** The
> inventory below was run: 10 handoffs per sample, **7.7% Jev-shaped** against the
> pre-registered 25% threshold, **7.7–10.8% across four seeds**, and 88.4% of
> checkable claims settled by `stat`, `git`, a file test or a re-run. Full write-up
> in `docs/SDE_CASCADE_SCOPING.md`; code in `sde_cascade/inventory.py`.
>
> **Stated precisely, because the margin is narrower than the headline:** the
> decision holds on the measured share and under either adversarial bound alone, on
> every seed. Stacking *both* bounds at once — assume every ambiguous statement is
> Jev-shaped AND strip the third of the code bucket whose only evidence is a
> non-path quoted token — gives 21.6–29.9%, which crosses 25% on 2 of 4 seeds. Code
> linter is the right call; "not a close call" is not.
>
> The best single check is *does every backticked path still resolve?*, and it
> covers **39.3%** of code claims — not the 84.9% the shape table suggests, which
> counts any quoted token. The prototype's real cost is false alarms, not coverage:
> the unresolved rate walked from 43% to 24% **without finding one extra file**,
> purely by learning that `~/DEV/` is the Mac layout, that cross-repo references are
> the common case, and that the SecondBrain vault is Mac-only. Fourth item
> measurement has moved down the map.

**1. `sde_cascade` — but scoped, and the scoping is the deliverable.**
The target surface is real and large: **126 `STATUS.md` files and 79 handoffs** in
`~/DEV`. The failure is live — on 2026-09-20 three documents asserted the running
header was stripped when it removed nothing, and this very file's sibling asserted
### Blocked on access, not on effort — and both share one unblock

- **`semantic_find`**: no Kitman or MyLink contract, quote or pricing document exists
  in `~/DEV`, on Drive (full depth, nine filename patterns), or in personal Gmail;
  the vault is Mac-only. The documents are almost certainly in **Baylor Outlook**,
  which is not connected.
- **`autoresearch_feature_discovery`**: the biggest genuine upside on this map
  (decomposition beat asking directly, RMSE 1.77 against 2.15) and governance is no
  longer the gate — but **there is no input corpus on this box.** Checked the Kitman
  injury export: 29 columns, and the only long fields are `Pathology`, which is a
  controlled clinical vocabulary rather than prose, and `Game Opposition`, which is
  team names. No narrative column at all. That is the PP_Recruiting finding repeating.

Both need access to a system that holds the prose — Kitman's narrative fields behind a
key that is not read-only, or Baylor Outlook. **One access conversation unblocks two
items**, which makes it worth more than either alone.

### Demoted on inspection

**`function_calling`** reads better on the map than it is. Claude Code already *is*
the natural-language-to-CLI layer, so routing a chat request through Jev adds a step
where a working one exists. The one place it is not redundant is the same place the
skill router paid off: **as a hook**, deciding without a conversation turn. Build it
only in that form, or not at all.

## Corrections to the 2026-09-19 chat answer

Four things the full read changed:

1. The 32k fit question is answered: 155 skills fit comfortably.
2. Citation checking is **not** ruled out for the TOS brief. See above.
3. Fireflies renaming is workable as *selection*: code or an LLM proposes 3 to 5
   candidate titles, Jev picks one. It still cannot write a title, and it is still
   gated on stripping athlete names from the summary.
4. Memory deduplication is the entity-alignment shape (a 3-level Score whose levels are
   the actions), not a Noul with a threshold.

> non-path quoted token — gives 21.6–29.9%, which crosses 25% on 2 of 4 seeds. Code
> linter is the right call; "not a close call" is not.
>
> The best single check is *does every backticked path still resolve?*, and it
> covers **39.3%** of code claims — not the 84.9% the shape table suggests, which
> counts any quoted token. The prototype's real cost is false alarms, not coverage:
> the unresolved rate walked from 43% to 24% **without finding one extra file**,
> purely by learning that `~/DEV/` is the Mac layout, that cross-repo references are
> the common case, and that the SecondBrain vault is Mac-only. Fourth item
> measurement has moved down the map.

**1. `sde_cascade` — but scoped, and the scoping is the deliverable.**
The target surface is real and large: **126 `STATUS.md` files and 79 handoffs** in
`~/DEV`. The failure is live — on 2026-09-20 three documents asserted the running
header was stripped when it removed nothing, and this very file's sibling asserted
### Blocked on access, not on effort — and both share one unblock

- **`semantic_find`**: no Kitman or MyLink contract, quote or pricing document exists
  in `~/DEV`, on Drive (full depth, nine filename patterns), or in personal Gmail;
  the vault is Mac-only. The documents are almost certainly in **Baylor Outlook**,
  which is not connected.
- **`autoresearch_feature_discovery`**: the biggest genuine upside on this map
  (decomposition beat asking directly, RMSE 1.77 against 2.15) and governance is no
  longer the gate — but **there is no input corpus on this box.** Checked the Kitman
  injury export: 29 columns, and the only long fields are `Pathology`, which is a
  controlled clinical vocabulary rather than prose, and `Game Opposition`, which is
  team names. No narrative column at all. That is the PP_Recruiting finding repeating.

Both need access to a system that holds the prose — Kitman's narrative fields behind a
key that is not read-only, or Baylor Outlook. **One access conversation unblocks two
items**, which makes it worth more than either alone.

### Demoted on inspection

**`function_calling`** reads better on the map than it is. Claude Code already *is*
the natural-language-to-CLI layer, so routing a chat request through Jev adds a step
where a working one exists. The one place it is not redundant is the same place the
skill router paid off: **as a hook**, deciding without a conversation turn. Build it
only in that form, or not at all.

## Corrections to the 2026-09-19 chat answer

Four things the full read changed:

1. The 32k fit question is answered: 155 skills fit comfortably.
2. Citation checking is **not** ruled out for the TOS brief. See above.
3. Fireflies renaming is workable as *selection*: code or an LLM proposes 3 to 5
   candidate titles, Jev picks one. It still cannot write a title, and it is still
   gated on stripping athlete names from the summary.
4. Memory deduplication is the entity-alignment shape (a 3-level Score whose levels are
   the actions), not a Noul with a threshold.

## Jev scouting report: RESEARCH and PROGRAM

Only three candidates pass all three gates, and two of them are in one repo: `SportScienceResearchRepo`. Most PROGRAM folders are empty stubs: OKRs_2026-27, NCAA_BestPractices_Doc, SPA_Presentation, Supervisor_Reviews (one update file), and AppliedNewsletter (one issue).

### Ranked candidates

**1. Domain tags for the Evidence Library (passes all 3 gates, effort S–M)**
- **Where:** `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\SportScienceResearchRepo\evidence-taxonomy.mjs` (`inferTaxonomy`, regex per label). `scripts/build-paper-taxonomy.mjs` writes its output to `paper-taxonomy.json`.
- **Judgment:** which of 8 domains, 7 audiences, 16 sports and a set of populations a paper belongs to. Could be one Choice per facet, or one Noul per label.
- **Data:** 707 published records. 407 of them still carry `taxonomySource: "rules-v1-unreviewed"`. 300 are human-reviewed (197 `full-text-screening`, 103 `zotero-paper-brief`), so a labelled eval set already exists.
- **Consumer:** the public library UI, `football-research-library.jsx`. Its Domain filter is at line 265, and it filters on `p.context.domains` at line 130.
- **Baseline and why it falls short:** I ran `inferTaxonomy` against the 300 reviewed records. Domain precision is 0.63, recall 0.77, and the full domain set matches exactly in only 55 of 300. "Rehabilitation & Return to Sport" is wrongly added 133 times. Patterns like `/\bperformance\b/` and `/\btreatment\b/` over-fire.
  - Caveat: reviewed records may have been reviewed using text the rules never see.
- **Not a re-proposal:** this is a different corpus (papers.json, 707 records, versus 1,418 Zotero records), a different taxonomy (8 domains versus 96 topics in 14 domains) and a different consumer. One check sets S versus M: if the papers.json IDs largely overlap the Zotero keys and the 14 Zotero domains map onto these 8, just reuse `TypeSafe_Sandbox/zotero_classify` results through a mapping table.

**2. Study-design triage for the screening queue (passes all 3 gates, effort M)**
- **Where:** `scripts/build-pilot-shortlist.mjs`, function `evidencePriority`, writes `docs/pilot-expansion-shortlist.json`.
- **Judgment:** a Choice over the 12 `studyDesign` labels the reviewers already use, plus a Noul on "not primary evidence (editorial, protocol, erratum)".
- **Data:** 1,534 source PDFs not yet in the library (`library-coverage-manifest.json`). Titles come from filenames, and some filenames are useless (e.g. `12-MON~1.PDF`). Full-text extraction already runs (`sourceVerification.extractedCharacters`), so first-page text can be the state sent to Jev.
- **Consumer:** the shortlist builder, which picks 12 papers per domain for human full-text screening. The records in `docs/pilot-screening/` are that screening's output.
- **Baseline:** title-regex points (+12 for a systematic review, and so on). Among the 197 screened records, 80 (41%) trigger no design pattern at all. That is despite the set being pre-selected by this same regex, so it is an optimistic figure.
- **Note:** a pure include/exclude screen has little leverage here. Only 5 of 204 screened papers were excluded.

**3. Athlete-data screening, one product at a time (passes all 3 gates; state is thin; effort S)**
- **Where:** `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\Tech_Inventory_Analysis\scripts\aliases.py`, `ATHLETE_DATA_CATEGORIES` (lines 283 and 494).
- **Judgment:** a few narrow Nouls per product: stores identifiable athlete data, stores health data, cloud-hosted. Weights combined in code.
- **Data:** 188 products and 75 current candidates.
- **Consumer:** the detailed second-pass form (STATUS Next #2: "75 athlete-data candidates, Recovery Record first").
- **Baseline:** being in a category flags the product. Every "performance" or "video-analytics" product gets flagged, and every comms or admin product is cleared, with no judgment on the product itself.
- **Weakness of the idea:** the state is little more than a vendor name and a unit. Best slotted into the post-29 September final run.

**On the survey free text you asked about:** yes, it is hand-coded. The open-ended field "What technology and software is your department currently using" is parsed through 827 lines of hand-written `aliases.py`. It is finished for this cycle: `clean/prose_responses_review.csv` has 1 row and `unmapped_review.csv` has 7. Re-coding it with Jev adds nothing now. The leverage is #3 and the next survey cycle.

**4. BAIR proposal rubric as a second reader (weak on volume, effort S)**
- **Where:** `BAIR_Steering_Committee/docs/program/framework-current-jan2026.md`.
- **Judgment:** one Score per dimension (5 weighted dimensions, weights 30/20/25/15/10) plus a Noul for the pass/fail feasibility gate. Textbook composite-scoring.
- **Consumer:** the `*_Scoring_Summary.docx` and Evaluation Report documents.
- **Problem:** there are only 4 proposals in `02_Proposals`. Its value is consistency checking (did two scorers disagree?), not throughput. Gate 1 passes, gate 2 passes, and volume fails.

### Near-misses (fail a gate)
- **Checking Ask the Library Decision Briefs** (`ask-library/pilot-core.mjs:557`): today it only checks that the excerpt appears word-for-word on the page, not that the excerpt supports the claim. That is the citation_check shape, which is already built. It also fails gate 2: STATUS shows the pilot dormant since the 2026-07-23 approval, with no briefs being produced.
- **Sport_Tech_Vetting:** the STRN rubric exists (`Quality_Framework_Sports_Technologies_Table.csv`), but there are no vendor documents to score and STATUS is empty. The Request_Tracker in SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework holds 2 requests, so tier/data-category assignment has no volume either.
- **Curriculum-to-competency mapping:** CPSS points to `AgentAssist/context/competencies.md`, but AgentAssist on this machine is a README only. There are 11 modules and nothing that consumes a mapping. Education_Alignment is strategy prose with no list of items to map.
- **Research in 5 role and evidence-level picks** (`Weekly_Research_Review/docs/CONTENT_SPEC.md:66`): one paper a week, already covered by the verifier.
- **Newsletter content selection, OKR grading, NCAA gap check:** no data on disk (one issue; OKR and NCAA folders are empty).

### Real volume
Items that exist in dozens or more are: #1 (407 records, plus more as the library grows), #2 (1,534 PDFs) and #3 (188 products). Everything else is one-off.
